subject.title: Feature request: first-class .env / environment-backed secret config UX

question: What SecretRef source metadata may Control UI and CLI expose for env-backed secrets, and should this issue remain the canonical tracker for the Control UI UX portion?
rationale: The code path is identifiable, but exposing env variable names, provider aliases, and resolution status is a product/security boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve Conservative Source-Aware UX
options.body: Show masked config/env/unset state and resolved/unresolved status, with env variable names shown only within a maintainer-approved disclosure boundary.

options.title: Consolidate With CLI Secret UX
options.body: Move the remaining Control UI requirements under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/16351 if maintainers want one broader config-secret UX tracker.

options.title: Defer UI Disclosure
options.body: Keep structured SecretRefs read-only and generic in Control UI until a later security review defines metadata disclosure rules.

recommendation.title: Approve Conservative Source-Aware UX
recommendation.body: Show masked config/env/unset state and resolved/unresolved status, with env variable names shown only within a maintainer-approved disclosure boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current affected Control UI/config lines and recent routing history point most strongly to this owner for the disclosure and product-boundary call.
